verdict: The type grammar has arrived — "860 *calories*" in display serif, the hairline ledgers with right-set serif values, the italic punch words are genuinely benchmark-level, and Home already runs card-free. But the pages are still engineered: every screen stacks a dense upper band and lets the remainder fall away as residue, so no frame has one subject — on Home the kept line (~46pt), the calorie figure (~68pt), and a ~50pt cocoa camera disc all claim first glance; on becoming the cover's lower two-thirds is unshaped void under a four-register text stack. Form controls keep puncturing the illusion — outlined mood capsules, two rounded text fields, a labeled three-icon tab pill, a hamburger on every masthead. The components are designed; the compositions are still assembled.

compositions.composition: THE KEPT PAGE — a one-sentence page. Tracked-caps date eyebrow alone at top. The vow at 64–72pt serif over two lines owning the upper half, hairline beneath stopping at a 40pt ✦ seal, one 15pt sub-line. The lower half is a single four-row receipt in beat-19 grammar — calories 860 of ~1,473 / protein 62 of 90g / overnight fast, counts tomorrow / steps 6,420 — hairlines full-width, serif values right-set. Nothing else on the page: one headline, one receipt, one seal.

THE CLOSING RECEIPT — centered gravity replaces the top-stack. "closing the day." as a centered serif couplet at ~52pt sitting at optical center (beat-19 placement), only the eyebrow above it. Below: the ledger (protein / tomorrow / plates still open), then "how did today feel?" as one hairline row of three bare serif words, then a bare rule for her one line. No second headline, no capsules, no field boxes — the whole page is one vertical receipt.

THE ISSUE COVER — her most recent plate photograph full-bleed from the top to a torn cream fold at ~55% height (the app owns real photography and currently shows none); masthead "becoming" in italic serif ~44pt set across the photo's lower edge, eyebrow beneath it on cream; the week's thesis at 64–76pt over the lower third; fore-edge ticks as vertical hairlines on the right edge. Photo-less fallback: pure type poster, headline alone at center field. (Captures 04/05 showed this same cover frame, so the spreads are directed by grammar: one figure or one number per spread, headline low, never two data blocks.)

TWO VOICES — a printed play script. Both measures narrowed to ~65% so cocoa-left and rose-right form two columns of color with a white river between; day markers as small centered tracked-caps dividers; jeni's opening line of each day set 4pt larger like a paragraph lead. Input is a bare baseline hairline with a deep-rose ✦ send mark. The masthead stays; the glitch fragment and duplicate pair go.

THE LETTER (capture 07 showed Home — the once-per-day gate held — so this is proposed from the app's own grammar): a full cream sheet with no tab bar. Eyebrow "FROM JENI · MONDAY", then the letter set in serif at 24–26pt with 1.6 leading and a wide 24pt margin, dated top-right in oldstyle numerals, signed "jeni ♥" in deep rose. It should look like a folded note photographed for a magazine — type only, one column, no interface at all.

checklist_iconic.diagnosis: The kept line is one quiet event among three louder ones: at ~46pt it is out-scaled by the 68pt calorie figure and out-inked by the cocoa camera disc; its seal is an 18pt ghost dingbat drifting past the end of a full-width hairline, illegible as a seal at screenshot distance; and the sub-caption hugs the hairline like form helper text. It currently reads as a section header above a dashboard — nothing about it says vow, and nothing about it invites the thumb or the screenshot.
checklist_iconic.proposal: THE VOW LINE — the day is one sentence set like a magazine dedication: 64–72pt serif over two lines, the punch word in italic Fraunces, beneath it a hairline that stops short and ends in a 40pt ✦ seal. The sentence IS the control — touch anywhere on it and the camera rises. Keeping it is the icon: the hairline draws itself left-to-right (0.6s trim animation), the ✦ fills deep rose and stamps with a soft haptic swell, and the sentence resets in italic as a signature. Kept days accumulate at the foot as a 15pt italic ledger, seal-first ("✦ walked after dinner" / "✦ snapped every plate") — her stack of vows. The screenshot is a giant serif vow, a wax seal, and the receipt of days she kept. All of it is SwiftUI text, a trim-animated line, and a scale/opacity stamp.

becoming_pageturn: Treat each page as a fixed printed sheet, not a scrolling surface, using plain scrollTransition/GeometryReader effects: (1) content parallax — headline and deck translate at ~0.85× scroll speed against the full-speed cream sheet, so type feels printed on moving paper; (2) turning shade — a 12pt vertical gradient of cocoa at 4–6% opacity rises on the trailing edge of the outgoing page and the leading edge of the incoming one, the shadow of a lifting leaf; (3) fore-edge detent — the right-edge vertical ticks advance with the swipe and the current tick lengthens 8→16pt and turns deep rose as the page commits; (4) pacing — .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging) with an overdamped spring (response ~0.45, damping ~0.9) so the settle feels like a page falling flat, plus exactly one soft haptic tick at commit, never mid-drag. No curl, no skeuomorphism: parallax + edge shade + detent + one tick is the print signal.
one_move: Make Home a one-sentence page: delete the camera disc and hamburger, demote 860 into the receipt ledger, and set the kept line at 64–72pt with the 40pt seal that draws itself when she keeps it — one giant serif vow above one quiet receipt. That single recomposition gives the app its reel frame (one subject, extreme typographic confidence, motion implied in a still) and every other screen inherits its law from it.
